## Independent integrated assessment

Inspected the entire three-file engineering diff from 9af7fcd9198471d044fec61f2c22f4fbcd781d7b to eff39535 on fix/npm-publication-visibility. This reviewer authored none of this fix, test or guidance. The user's exact bounded bugfix authorization and existing Release REL-SR-12/14/15/23, Runtime observation/retry and temporal/failure scenarios govern. Plan is null and work is empty; no new planned Design/Delivery package or milestone is selected. Prior initiative assessments are not substituted for this fresh final review.

The change increases only npm post-write observation to121 attempts. With the unchanged provider min(2**attempt,10) backoff this is120 waits,1175 seconds of sleep, plus actual observation time. The README's roughly20-minute wording is appropriately approximate; the existing executor job is bounded to60 minutes. Tag/GitHub observation remains6 attempts. Matching/conflicting observations exit immediately. Publication remains outside the loop, so delayed visibility never triggers an extra publish within the attempt. Exhaustion continues through the unchanged event, uncertain-write, persistence and actionable recovery failure path. Existing identity matching, public smoke, final re-observation, approval validation and immutable-candidate checks are unchanged.

The regression drives the actual executor with substituted public services: after npm is written,120 observations remain absent, the121st matches, waits equal0..119 and writes are exactly tag/GitHub/npm once. It fails under the old6-observation code and passes under the corrected code; this is outcome proof rather than only testing a constant. Existing40-test execution/coordination evidence retains conflict, timeout/lost-response, public-smoke failure, uncertain state, identity/authorization and persistence coverage. No successful public release or real npm availability guarantee is inferred.

## First-pass checklist

1. Spec alignment: pass — bounded observation supports the existing delayed-visibility/no-duplicate contract and exact user direction.
2. Test coverage: pass — same regression fails before and passes after, reaches the new final poll and observes single-write/completion behavior; retained broader suite passed.
3. Edge cases: pass — early match/conflict, exhaustion and non-npm limits retain existing control flow; delayed npm success now fits the longer bound.
4. Error handling: pass — unavailable/conflicting result remains incomplete with observed state saved; no failure becomes a fabricated pass.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass — no new runner, publication path, provider policy or evidence owner.
6. Compatibility: pass — only npm waiting budget changes; other boundaries, identities and command surfaces stay intact.
7. Security/privacy: pass — no secret/log/authentication expansion or repeated write; candidate-bound permissions remain unchanged.
8. Derived artifact currency: pass within scope — no generated/package/resource input change; a future release still builds and approves its own candidate.
9. Unrelated changes: pass — exact executor limit, meaningful regression and short guidance only.
10. Validation evidence: pass — red/green and retained40-test execution/coordination outputs inspected; independent focused rerun passed; no hosted CI/Verify claim.

Independently ran PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m unittest release_execution_tests.ReleaseExecutorTests.test_delayed_npm_visibility_completes_without_duplicate_publication:1test passed in2.167s. git diff --check passed. Inspected retained red.log failure at the old npm visibility timeout, green.log1-test success and suite.log40 tests passed in48.562s; implementation evidence records their exact scope and identities. No live publication or actual20-minute sleep was performed by the substituted test.

Current source and test identities are the exact reviewed basis below. Supporting provider/workflow reads establish backoff and job-budget context only; they are not a broader provider or hosted-setup approval.
